p2plus.recommendation: Replace with the canon warm-ink shadow (SHADOW[2] = 0 0.5rem 1.5rem rgba(64,59,54,0.14)) in rem, dropping the orange glow, or if a colored lift is desired keep it subtle and tokenized.

p2plus.title: Privacy/terms rely on fixed px sizing with no responsive hooks; only clamp() saves them at small widths
p2plus.recommendation: Optionally adopt useIsMobile to bump body copy to ~1rem and tighten list padding on phones; at minimum verify the 12px uppercase eyebrow remains legible at 320px width. Not blocking.

p2plus.title: Commitment panel gradient uses an untokenized #3D3D3A stop
p2plus.recommendation: Either use a solid C.charcoal like the footer/CTA, or make the two stops a tokenized pair (e.g. inkSoft #403B36 → charcoal) so dark surfaces stay consistent and on-palette.

p2plus.title: Inconsistent content max-width and back-affordance across the four legal pages
p2plus.recommendation: Standardize a prose measure (~760/42rem for text pages) and reuse the same nav back-chip on all text-heavy legal pages; keep the wider measure only for security's card grid intentionally.

p2plus.title: Legal pages ignore useIsMobile/useIsCompact and rely on clamp()/vw for responsiveness
p2plus.recommendation: Align privacy/terms/data-deletion with security/page.tsx: import useIsMobile/useIsCompact, convert to rem, and bump nav icon targets to ≥2.75rem.

p2plus.title: data-deletion container has no full-width outer wrapper; safe-area padding sits on the 720px centered box
p2plus.recommendation: Prioritize the i18n/nav conversion; optionally reduce side padding on very small phones via useIsSmall if 2rem feels tight at 320px.

p2plus.title: Security auto-fit minmax(250px) grid can overflow at 320px causing horizontal scroll
p2plus.recommendation: Keep aria-hidden on decorative SVGs and the visible <h3> labels (no a11y action needed); consider minmax(0,1fr) fallback on the smallest phones to avoid 250px + 2× padding exceeding 320px.

strengths: privacy, terms and security are fully internationalized: every user-facing string uses useTranslation, and all keys (dataBreachNotificationTitle, section10P2 with {link}, commitmentTitle2, etc.) are present across en/nl/de/es/fr — verified in messages/*.json.

privacy, terms and security share a genuinely cohesive header system (sticky blurred nav, back-chip, PalaceLogo, brand lockup, language selector) and a repeatable LEGAL-overline → display H1 → lastUpdated → Section/P/Ul/Li scaffold, giving three of four pages strong internal consistency.
security.tsx shows real polish: bespoke per-category and per-item SVG icon sets, a hero shield, a commitment dove, and warm gradient bands — a well-considered, on-brand illustrative layer.
Typography is consistently on-canon: all four pages use F.display 'Fraunces' for headings/brand and F.body 'Source Sans 3' for body, matching the display-serif + body-sans pairing.

security/page.tsx correctly follows canon: useIsMobile/useIsSmall hooks for inline responsiveness, aria-hidden on decorative SVGs, aria-labels on nav/language controls, and a safe ItemIcon fallback (categoryIcons[index] || <svg/>) that never crashes on out-of-range index.

Responsiveness stays inline-style only with no @media anywhere, honoring the iOS-seal inline-styling rule; external links use rel='noopener noreferrer', and language changes correctly skip cookies on native iOS (isNative guard) honoring Apple 5.1.2i.

Terms InlineLink MARKER pattern is robust: t() interpolates {email}/{link} → @@LINK@@ then splits, and all 5 locale JSONs preserve the placeholders, so links render correctly in every language with no orphaned markers.

All internal routes referenced resolve (/login, /security, /terms, /privacy, /register, /palace/keps); no broken Next.js Link targets found. Every t() key used by privacy/terms/security was verified present in en.json, with English→raw-key fallback so no hard render failures from missing keys.

Safe-area insets (env(safe-area-inset-*)) are respected on privacy and data-deletion, showing iOS notch awareness, and reusable styled sub-components (Section/P/Ul/Li, InlineLink) keep spacing/color decisions centralized per page.
